anomalies.observed: The anodes of D2, D23, and D39 are all tied to net /NET0086, which has no other connections. No supply or pull-up is present on this net.
anomalies.expected: The common anode net should be connected to a positive supply rail (e.g., +3V3) so that the LEDs can illuminate when their cathodes are pulled low by their respective drivers.
anomalies.impact: D2, D23, and D39 will never light, removing their status indication function from the board.

anomalies.observed: SW1 is a 2-position DIP switch. Pin 1 connects to R13 (120R to CAN0_L), pin 2 to R101 (120R to CAN1_L), pin 3 to CAN1_H (/NET0158), and pin 4 to CAN0_H (/NET0043). With standard SW_DIP_x02 pin pairing (1-2 and 3-4), closing switch 2 connects CAN0_H to CAN1_H directly, and closing switch 1 connects CAN0_L to CAN1_L through two 120R resistors.
anomalies.expected: Each CAN bus should have its own independent termination network, typically a 120R resistor between CAN_H and CAN_L controlled by a switch or jumper. The DIP switch should not bridge the two separate CAN buses.
anomalies.impact: Closing SW1 can short the two CAN buses together (CAN0_H to CAN1_H directly, and CAN0_L to CAN1_L through 240R), causing bus contention and communication failure instead of independent termination.

anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U44 and U48 have their logic-side ground (GND1, pin 4) and bus-side ground (GND2, pin 5) both connected to the common GND net.
anomalies.expected: For an isolated CAN bus, GND1 and GND2 must be separate nets (e.g., logic ground and isolated bus ground) to maintain galvanic isolation between the controller side and the bus side.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The isolation barrier is bypassed because both sides share the same ground. The CAN buses are not galvanically isolated, defeating the intended isolation and exposing the controller side to bus-side transients and ground loops.

parsed.summary: The design files contain several anomalies. The most clear-cut are three status LEDs (D2, D23, D39) whose anodes are left floating on /NET0086, the CAN termination DIP switch SW1 miswired so it bridges CAN0 and CAN1, and the isolated CAN transceivers U44/U48 having their isolated grounds tied together on GND, defeating the specified isolation.
